title: Continual Learning for AI Agents: From Failures to Durable Improvements - Soheil Feizi, RELAI
talk_summary: Soheil Feizi argues that agent improvement should be verifiable continual learning: turn production failures into replayable, graded learning environments, route each fix to the cheapest layer (memory, harness, or model), and require regression checks so old behavior doesn't break. He frames four principles—replayability, holisticness, lifelongness, efficiency—and demos a support-agent benchmark with regression traps.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of treating a bad session log plus feedback as the learning signal, they lift it into an executable simulation with mock/real tools, synthetic users, and explicit evaluators, so candidate fixes can be rerun and scored.
takeaways.evidence_quote: production logs are not learning environments. We need to transform them into replayable learning environments

takeaways.what_they_do: A fix is only accepted if it improves the new failing case AND prior passing cases still pass; regression is enforced inside the optimization loop, not checked afterward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every fix is proven to help and proven to break nothing that already worked

takeaways.technique: Route fix to smallest durable layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Root-cause the failure and choose the cheapest layer that explains it: memory fact/skill, harness (prompt/tool/workflow), or model weights—rather than defaulting to fine-tuning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A good learning engine should ask for the smallest durable change at the right layer of the agent.

takeaways.what_they_do: Compress a successful trajectory into a reusable how-to skill so the agent doesn't rediscover it; cheapest and fastest update layer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: skill distillation that compresses successful trajectory into reusable how-to do skill

takeaways.what_they_do: Ask a coding agent to analyze a log and edit the harness directly; flexible but unverified and prone to hidden regressions unless paired with replayable tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it is wipe-based. We don't know if even for that particular uh sample, if the change is effective, because it is not testable

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate a simulation (personas, intents, mock tools, evaluators) from a single instruction to test agent behavior on scenarios you have no logs for yet.
takeaways.evidence_quote: simply we can create a learning environment using such instruction
takeaways.numbers: score rose from 87% to 97% after one optimize loop on their demo
